answer: For a dawn poll on a canyon mirror, the server checks that each ballot has a distinct funded $10 deposit and rejects unfunded or reused deposits. Anyone may challenge two ballots as belonging to one person. A judge reviews the evidence; if persuaded, both ballots are discarded and their deposits go to the challenger; otherwise they remain. Each extra ballot ties up $10 and risks forfeiture. Duplicates may go unchallenged, and judges can err.
